segments.label: Historical heading
segments.original:
CAP. XCIX.
EDITTO
Sopra la denuncia degl’ Infermi.
segments.english:
Chapter 99
Edict
On reporting the sick

segments.label: Reporting duty
segments.original: Si riduce à memoria di qualsiuoglia persona l’ordine dato col Bando publicato sotto li 20. Giugno prossimo passato, che quando si scuopra in alcuna Casa, Monastero, ò altro luogo nella Città di Roma alcun’Infermo, ancorche l’infermità non dia segno, ò sospetto alcuno di Contagio, debbano li habitanti, e coabitanti denunciarlo al Notaro del Rione.
segments.english: Everyone is reminded of the order given in the proclamation published on 20 June last: whenever a sick person is discovered in any house, monastery, or other place in the city of Rome, even though the illness gives no sign or suspicion of contagion, the residents and co-residents must report that person to the district notary.

segments.label: Co-resident exception and penalties
segments.original: Dichiarando, che quando vno delli detti coabitanti hauerà date le denuncie, gli altri coabitanti saranno disobligati dal denunciare il medesimo, si come s’è ordinato nel Bando sudetto, alle cui pene si procederà irremissibilmente contro li trasgressori.
segments.english: It is clarified that when one of those co-residents has submitted the reports, the other co-residents are released from the obligation to report the same person, as was ordered in the aforesaid proclamation. The penalties prescribed in that proclamation are to be applied to offenders without remission.

notes.text: This is the Italian text printed in Gastaldi’s 1684 edition, reproducing an edict dated 24 August 1656. The heading and substantive text are Italian; CAP. and Dat. are conventional abbreviated formulae. The facsimile documents this printed edition rather than an independently authenticated 1656 broadside.

The proclamation of 20 June 1656 expressly recalled here is reproduced in chapter 55. Its §1, printed page 297 (scan 381), requires immediate reporting, specified information about the illness and the physician, and a faithful and lawful report for the co-resident exemption. Those details are not repeated in chapter 99. The earlier proclamation’s date appears on printed page 301 (scan 385).

Denunciare is rendered as “report”: it denotes an official notification here, rather than necessarily an accusation. Denuncie is plural in the printed second sentence. Rione is rendered as “district”; Notaro del Rione identifies the district notary who receives the notification.

Il medesimo (“the same person”) refers back to the sick person. The exemption concerns other co-residents reporting that same person; it does not discharge all future reporting duties or the separate duties of clergy and physicians. Chapter 55, §4, expressly requires clergy to report even when someone else has already reported the case.

Irremissibilmente is rendered as “without remission.” The edict invokes the earlier proclamation’s penalties without restating them. This is a threat of enforcement in the prescribed rule, not evidence that the penalties were imposed in every case.
